screenshots.shows: The tray icon's menu, open: Pause cleaning, the three convert checkboxes and Start with Windows, Open config location, a separator, Exit; no plugin items

steps: Deploy the working tree first: the script refuses a running build older than src/TrayApplicationContext.cs, which builds the menu.
No plugins installed, so the menu shows only the built-in items. A plugin in the install folder's plugins/ adds a checkbox per plugin, which would put it in the frame.

Checkmarks are the capturing machine's own settings. As first shot: Convert paths, Convert numbers, Convert placeholders and Start with Windows on, Pause cleaning off. A fresh install ships the three convert features off.

The script posts NotifyIcon's hidden window its tray callback message with WM_RBUTTONUP, which runs NotifyIcon's own ShowContextMenu, so the frame is the menu a right-click opens. It places the pointer near the primary display's tray corner first, since the menu opens at the pointer, and puts it back afterwards.
Captured with window-shot.ps1 -Method Alpha -Popup from the docs-relevance skill, so the backdrops never take focus and the dropdown stays open.
No item may be highlighted: a highlighted row means the pointer entered the menu.
No frame step: the ToolStrip dropdown is square and opaque and draws its own 1px grey border on all four sides.
